result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): B keeps every question on real past experience, and its 'swap these leading questions' table helps a first-time interviewer. Its spoken consent script is thorough on recording but never says 'I'm not selling anything' out loud. A does say that in its opening, but its 'light concept check' section asks hypothetical questions about Paddlepoint, and 'most frustrating part' nudges the participant toward a negative answer. Both screenshots cut off at the bottom, so neither clearly fits on one printed page. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A's questions are tightly anchored in past behaviour, with neutral probes, a 'swap these leading questions' table and timings that add to 40 (3+5+20+7+5). However, its spoken opener never says the interviewer isn't selling anything; that point appears only in a note to the interviewer. B's opener covers consent, 'no right answers' and 'not selling', and its times also total 40, but its concept-check section asks hypothetical questions and some wording is leading or closed ('most frustrating part', 'Ever shown up and it didn't work out?'). Both pages appear to run slightly past one screen, so a single printed page isn't certain for either.
